absent: Locking discipline and concurrency rules for event queues and ioctl handling are not shown.
State machines for key repeat timing and force feedback upload playback erasure plus gain and autocenter interaction are not shown.

Event mask filtering semantics plus grab and revoke ownership transitions and clock selection effects on timestamps are not shown.
Valid ranges for absolute axis fuzz flat and resolution plus multitouch blob tracking and tool lifecycle rules are not shown.
Bus assignment rules plus device identity allocation and version negotiation beyond numeric values are not shown.

Structure input_event carries timestamp information followed by type as 16 bit unsigned and code as 16 bit unsigned and value as 32 bit signed. Timestamp storage has a legacy timeval layout in one build configuration and separate seconds plus microseconds words in another with a sparc 64 bit variant using padding. Aliases input_event_sec and input_event_usec expose seconds and microseconds across layouts.

Structure input_id orders bustype and vendor and product and version each as 16 bit unsigned. Structure input_absinfo orders value and minimum and maximum and fuzz and flat and resolution each as 32 bit signed.

Structure input_keymap_entry orders flags and len as single bytes with index as 16 bit unsigned and keycode as 32 bit unsigned and scancode as 32 bytes. Constant INPUT_KEYMAP_BY_INDEX marks lookup by index. Structure input_mask orders type and codes_size as 32 bit unsigned with codes_ptr as 64 bit address.

Basic device queries use group E numbers 0x01 through 0x09. EVIOCGVERSION uses 0x01 to return driver version as integer and EVIOCGID uses 0x02 to return device identity and EVIOCGREP with EVIOCSREP share 0x03 to fetch and store repeat settings as two unsigned integers. EVIOCGKEYCODE with EVIOCGKEYCODE_V2 share get on 0x04 and EVIOCSKEYCODE with EVIOCSKEYCODE_V2 share set on 0x04 with legacy integer pair versus keymap entry forms. EVIOCGNAME uses 0x06 and EVIOCGPHYS uses 0x07 and EVIOCGUNIQ uses 0x08 and EVIOCGPROP uses 0x09 each with caller length for name and location and identifier and properties.

State queries use variable length reads. EVIOCGMTSLOTS uses 0x0a for multitouch slot state. EVIOCGKEY uses 0x18 and EVIOCGLED uses 0x19 and EVIOCGSND uses 0x1a and EVIOCGSW uses 0x1b for global key plus indicator plus sound plus switch state. EVIOCGBIT adds event number to base 0x20 for capability bits. EVIOCGABS adds axis number to base 0x40 to fetch axis description while EVIOCSABS adds axis number to base 0xc0 to store axis description.

Force feedback uses EVIOCSFF at 0x80 to submit an effect descriptor and EVIOCRMFF at 0x81 to erase by integer identifier and EVIOCGEFFECTS at 0x84 to report simultaneous effect count as integer. Exclusive access uses EVIOCGRAB at 0x90 and revocation uses EVIOCREVOKE at 0x91 each with integer argument. Filtering uses EVIOCGMASK at 0x92 to fetch and EVIOCSMASK at 0x93 to store a mask descriptor. Clock selection uses EVIOCSCLOCKID at 0xa0 with integer clock identifier.

Identity indices use ID_BUS at zero and ID_VENDOR at one and ID_PRODUCT at two and ID_VERSION at three. Descriptor ff_replay orders length and delay as 16 bit unsigned. Descriptor ff_trigger orders button and interval as 16 bit unsigned. Descriptor ff_envelope orders attack_length and attack_level and fade_length and fade_level as 16 bit unsigned. Descriptor ff_constant_effect pairs signed level with an envelope. Descriptor ff_ramp_effect pairs signed start_level and signed end_level with an envelope. Descriptor ff_condition_effect orders right_saturation and left_saturation as unsigned with right_coeff and left_coeff as signed plus deadband as unsigned and center as signed.

Descriptor ff_periodic_effect orders waveform and period as unsigned with magnitude and offset as signed and phase as unsigned plus envelope with custom_len as 32 bit unsigned and custom_data as user pointer to signed samples. Descriptor ff_rumble_effect orders strong_magnitude and weak_magnitude as 16 bit unsigned. Descriptor ff_haptic_effect orders hid_usage and vendor_id as 16 bit unsigned with vendor_waveform_page as single byte plus intensity and repeat_count and retrigger_period as 16 bit unsigned. Descriptor ff_effect orders type as 16 bit unsigned with id as 16 bit signed and direction as 16 bit unsigned plus trigger and replay with a variant of constant or ramp or periodic or two condition entries or rumble or haptic.

EV_VERSION advertises event protocol version as 0x010001 for compatibility checks between user space and driver.
The user input header uses guard macro _UAPI_INPUT_H to prevent repeated inclusion.

Shared values use BTN_TRIGGER_HAPPY equal to BTN_TRIGGER_HAPPY1 with SW_RADIO equal to SW_RFKILL_ALL and KEY_MIN_INTERESTING equal to KEY_MUTE and FF_EFFECT_MIN equal to FF_HAPTIC with FF_EFFECT_MAX equal to FF_RAMP and FF_WAVEFORM_MIN equal to FF_SQUARE with FF_WAVEFORM_MAX equal to FF_CUSTOM.

Timestamp layout in input_event varies with word size and 64 bit time selection and kernel versus user build and sparc 64 bit padding, so consumers must use input_event_sec with input_event_usec rather than fixed offsets. Assuming timeval size or field positions risks misreading type plus code plus value on other builds.
